_meta.disclaimer: Synthetic demonstration data for SIH26189 prototype. All cases, evidence, and notes are fictional and do not represent real criminal investigations.

cases.title: Koramangala Network Anomaly Investigation
cases.description: Investigation into anomalous activity detected in Community 4, centred on 10 entities (P201–P210) with elevated anomaly scores. All 10 entities exhibit MODERATE risk band and high communication burst patterns.

cases.title: Bridge Entity Network Analysis
cases.description: Analysis of high-betweenness entities in Community 2 that act as bridges to other communities. P138 (betweenness 0.109) and P158 (betweenness 0.107) connect otherwise separate clusters.

cases.title: Cross-Community Communication Patterns
cases.description: Monitoring communication patterns between Community 3 entities and external communities. P217 (betweenness 0.109) shows significant cross-community connectivity.

evidence.title: Highest anomaly score in network
evidence.description: Entity P202 exhibits the highest anomaly score (50) in the entire network, with betweenness centrality of 0.110.

evidence.title: Communication burst pattern detected
evidence.description: P202 recorded a maximum daily burst of 24 events in a single day, the highest in the network, across 16 active days.

evidence.title: All 10 entities in single community
evidence.description: All 10 highest-anomaly entities (P201–P210) belong to Community 4, which contains exactly 10 entities — suggesting a tightly connected anomalous cluster.

evidence.title: FIR naming entity from linked network
evidence.description: SYN-FIR-001 describes a robbery at Koramangala, Bengaluru. Vikram Patel identified as accused under Section 303 BNS. Koramangala is a shared location with SYN-FIR-012.

evidence.title: Repeated entity appearance across FIRs
evidence.description: Vikram Patel appears as accused in both SYN-FIR-001 and SYN-FIR-012, across different incident types. Rajesh Sharma appears in both as complainant/witness.

evidence.title: Elevated transaction activity
evidence.description: P201 recorded 30 transactions with 39 unique contacts — disproportionate for a single entity.

evidence.title: Highest betweenness in Community 2
evidence.description: P138 has betweenness centrality of 0.109, the highest in Community 2, with only 24 connections — suggesting a strategic bridging role.

evidence.title: Second bridge entity in Community 2
evidence.description: P158 shows betweenness centrality of 0.107 with 21 connections, forming a dual-bridge pattern with P138.

evidence.title: P047 cross-community connectivity
evidence.description: P047 has 7 connections with betweenness 0.011, linking Community 0 entities to Community 2.

evidence.title: FIR referencing bridge-area entities
evidence.description: SYN-FIR-010 describes misappropriation at MG Road, Jaipur. Ravi Kumar identified as accused.

evidence.title: P217 highest betweenness in Community 3
evidence.description: P217 has betweenness centrality of 0.109 with 30 connections, serving as the primary bridge from Community 3.

evidence.title: High call volume to external communities
evidence.description: P217 recorded 12 calls, 14 messages, and 3 meetings — unusually high for Community 3.

evidence.title: FIR documenting location overlap
evidence.description: SYN-FIR-003 filed at Koramangala PS. Deepa Nair identified as accused under Section 351 BNS.

notes.author: Investigator A
notes.content: P202 shows the highest anomaly score in the entire network. Recommend priority surveillance of this entity and its immediate contacts in Community 4.

notes.author: Investigator A
notes.content: Community 4 is unusually small (only 10 entities) but all have MODERATE risk. This suggests either a specialised cell or a tightly controlled network structure.

notes.author: Investigator A
notes.content: Cross-referencing P201's transaction count with temporal data shows clustering around Sep 1–5. Burst detection flagged this period.

notes.author: Investigator B
notes.content: P138's high betweenness with relatively low degree (24) indicates it serves as a critical information broker between Community 2 and the rest of the network.

notes.author: Investigator B
notes.content: P158 and P138 together account for most of Community 2's external connectivity. Removing either would significantly fragment the community.

notes.author: Investigator A
notes.content: P217's cross-community links warrant closer monitoring. Communication volume is 3x the Community 3 average.
